newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end higher, seen attacking 1,200.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end higher, seen attacking 1,200.

text.p: Austrian shares ended firmer on Wednesday and traders were unanimous in predicting the ATX index of 21 blue chips would head for 1,200 points this week.
"The 1,200 point level is in sight," one trader said. "Confidence in the market has picked up again," said another.
The index climbed 6.03 points or 0.51 percent to 1,187.01. Among its constituents nine shares rose, six fell and two were unchanged.
Trade was concentrated in oil and chemicals group OMV, engineering group VA Technologie and fireproof materials maker Radex, traders said.

OMV rose after reporting a 39 percent preliminary increase in 1996 pre-tax earnings but came under pressure from profit taking, closing 6.6 schillings lower at 1,322.90. Radex also ended 7.85 schillings higher at 396 after posting a 24 percent net profit increase for 1996.
The session's top gainer was microchip maker AMS, gaining 3.86 percent to 1,049 schillings.
The leading decliner was VA Technologie, falling 2.46 percent to 1,110 schillings.
The February ATX future rose 1.6 points to 1,186.1.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index added 1.28 points or 0.29 percent to 442.74.
